html:
The Shek Kip Mei fire broke out on Christmas night 1953 in a squatter settlement in Kowloon, Hong Kong, and left about 53,000 people homeless.

After the communist victory in the Chinese Civil War in 1949, refugees flooded into Hong Kong, and hundreds of thousands lived in shacks on the hillsides. The refugees also brought capital and skills from Shanghai, and the colony began to make textiles, toys and plastics for export.

The fire pushed the British government to build cheap resettlement blocks, the start of the largest public housing programme in the world outside socialist states. Today nearly half of Hong Kong's people live in public rental or subsidised flats. The housing helped keep wages low and factories busy, but it did not end tension, as the riots of 1967 showed. Film makers from Shanghai who came in these years laid the base of Hong Kong cinema.
sum: The Shek Kip Mei fire broke out on Christmas night 1953 in a squatter settlement in Kowloon, Hong Kong, and left about 53,000 people homeless.
